title: Agent Skills Just Became an Open Standard - Learn It Now
content:
One million published skills, and nearly two hundred eighty million installs.
If you work with AI agents, this is a skill you should learn this weekend.
On October twenty second, Anthropic donated Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation, which sits under the Linux Foundation.
That is the same foundation that already looks after MCP, the Model Context Protocol.
The foundation also added Open Responses from OpenAI, OpenEnv from Hugging Face, and OpenSandbox from Alibaba.
So the big labs are agreeing on shared building blocks for agents.
So what exactly is a skill?
A skill is just a folder.
Inside it there is a file called SKILL dot M D. It teaches an agent how to do one specific task.
It can also hold scripts and reference material the agent needs.
The agent first reads only the name and description, and opens the full instructions when the task matches.
According to Anthropic, more than seventy agent platforms have integrated it, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and VS Code.
That means one skill you write can travel across many tools.
Why does this matter for your career?
Because companies do not just need a smart model. They need the model to follow their process.
Say a company wants its agent to prepare client reports exactly the way the team does today.
Someone has to write that process down as a skill, test it, and fix it when it fails. That someone could be you.
Here is how to start.
Pick one task you repeat every week.
Write a SKILL file with a clear description of when to use it and the exact steps.
Add one good example, then test it and improve it.
And before installing skills from strangers, read the scripts first. Anthropic's own guidance says to audit unfamiliar code.
Here's my take. Prompting was the first skill. Writing reusable skills for agents is the next one.
Put three good skills on GitHub, and you have a portfolio that shows you understand real work.
Comment SKILLS on Instagram and I'll send you the link, or grab it in the LinkedIn post.
Follow for your daily AI update.
